chunks: Al-Hasan ibn 'Ali al-Washsha' narrated from Ahmad ibn 'Umar, who said:
I asked him about the saying of Allah, Mighty and Majestic:
"Two just ones from among you, or two others from outside you."

He said: "The two from among you are two Muslims, and the two from outside you are from the People of the Book. If you do not find any from the People of the Book, then from the Magians, because the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله said: 'Apply to them the sunnah of the People of the Book.' And that is when a man dies in a foreign land and does not find two Muslims to make them witnesses; then two men from the People of the Book [may serve]."

key_terms.أَهْلِ الْكِتَابِ: the People of the Book accepted here as substitute witnesses
key_terms.الْمَجُوسِ: the Magians, treated in this context like the People of the Book
key_terms.بِأَرْضِ غُرْبَةٍ: in a foreign land away from one's community
key_terms.سُنُّوا بِهِمْ سُنَّةَ أَهْلِ الْكِتَابِ: treat them according to the legal precedent applied to the People of the Book

ai.seo_question: Who can serve as witnesses according to the verse "ذَوَا عَدْلٍ مِنْكُمْ أَوْ آخَرَانِ مِنْ غَيْرِكُمْ"?
ai.summary: This hadith explains the Qur'anic phrase about witnesses by identifying "from among you" as Muslims and "from outside you" as members of the People of the Book. It further states that if such witnesses are unavailable, Magians may be accepted, especially in the case of death occurring in a foreign land where Muslim witnesses cannot be found.
